seo.title: AI Overviews vs Featured Snippets: What's the Difference?
seo.meta_description: AI Overviews vs featured snippets: how each is built, how sources are chosen and shown, how clicks are counted, and how to optimize for both at once.

h1: AI Overviews vs Featured Snippets: What Changed and What to Do
answer: In AI Overviews vs featured snippets, the core difference is that a featured snippet quotes one page as the answer, while an AI Overview writes a new summary, often drawing on several pages found through related searches, and links to multiple sources. Both reward direct answers and clear structure, so one well-built page can win in both.
key_takeaways: Featured snippets quote one page; AI Overviews summarize several.
AI Overviews can use related searches across subtopics to build an answer.
Both need a page that is indexed and eligible for a snippet.
Direct answers, question headings and lists help in both.
Clicks from both are counted in Search Console's web search totals.

sections.heading: Featured snippets in brief
sections.body_html:
A featured snippet is a highlighted box at the top of some Google results that quotes a short passage from one page, with a link to it. Google picks the passage it judges best answers the query, often a paragraph, list or table. For years, winning the snippet was the main goal of answer engine optimization.

Snippets still exist, and the habits that win them, such as answering the question directly near the top of a page, remain useful.

sections.heading: AI Overviews in brief
sections.body_html:
AI Overviews are AI-generated summaries that appear at the top of some results. Instead of quoting one page, Google writes a new answer from information across several sources and shows links to those sources. Google describes a technique it calls query fan-out, issuing multiple related searches across subtopics and data sources to build the response. AI Overviews are shown when Google judges they add value beyond the standard results, especially for complex or multi-part questions.

Google reported in July 2025 that AI Overviews were used by more than 2 billion people a month.

sections.heading: Side-by-side comparison
sections.body_html:
Featured snippetAI Overview
What appearsA quoted passage from one pageA newly written summary
Number of sourcesOneUsually several, shown as links
How sources are foundRanking results for the queryThe query plus related searches across subtopics
Best contentA concise answer blockClear answers to the main question and its follow-ups
Controlsnosnippet, max-snippetThe same snippet controls
ReportingSearch Console web resultsIncluded in Search Console web results

sections.heading: What both reward
sections.body_html:
• Indexing and snippet eligibility. A page that cannot show a snippet cannot be used for either.
  • Direct answers to the exact question near the top.
  • Descriptive headings that match how people ask.
  • Lists and tables for steps, options and comparisons.
  • Helpful, reliable content with visible expertise.

If you have optimized for snippets, you have a head start on AI Overviews.

sections.heading: Where AI Overviews ask for more
sections.body_html:
Because AI Overviews can draw on several related searches, pages that cover the natural follow-up questions get more chances to be linked. A page about "how much does a GEO audit cost" that also answers what drives price, what is included and how long it takes can be useful for several parts of one overview. Featured snippets rarely reward that breadth; AI Overviews often do.

AI Overviews also benefit from specific, checkable facts, since Google is combining information and needs passages it can trust.

sections.heading: How clicks are counted
sections.body_html:
Google includes clicks and impressions from AI features in the standard web search totals in Search Console, rather than reporting them as a separate type. Featured snippet appearances are also part of web results. That means you will not see a neat "AI Overview clicks" line. Instead, watch impressions and clicks for the pages and question-style queries you optimized, and compare trends before and after changes.

Google has said that clicks from search results pages with AI Overviews tend to be higher quality, with visitors more likely to spend time on the site. Test that against your own engagement and lead data.

sections.heading: How to optimize one page for both
sections.body_html:
1. Open with a 40–60 word answer to the main question.
  2. Add a short list or table right after it if the answer has steps or options.
  3. Give each follow-up question its own heading and a two-to-four sentence answer.
  4. Back key facts with sources and dates.
  5. Close with an FAQ for smaller questions.
  6. Check snippet eligibility: no nosnippet, no overly short max-snippet, page indexed.

sections.heading: When to use snippet controls
sections.body_html: Snippet controls such as nosnippet, max-snippet and data-nosnippet limit how much of your text Google can show, and they apply to AI features too. Use them only for content you genuinely do not want quoted, such as paid material. For pages you want cited, leave snippets unrestricted. Google-Extended, by contrast, does not control AI Overviews; Google says it does not affect Search.

sections.heading: An example page that serves both
sections.body_html: Take the question "How long does GEO take to work?". A page built for both formats opens with: "Most GEO programs see first citations within one to three months, and broader visibility over three to six months as pages are indexed and authority grows." That sentence is a ready-made featured snippet. Below it, sections answer the follow-ups: what moves first, what slows things down, how to speed it up and how to measure progress. Those give an AI Overview several passages to draw on for the related searches it runs. One page, two chances to appear at the top of the results.

sections.heading: Which matters more now?
sections.body_html: Both matter, and they reward the same core habits. AI Overviews appear more often for complex, research-style questions, the kind buyers ask before choosing a provider, so they are especially important for service businesses. Featured snippets still win quick factual queries. Optimizing one page well usually serves both.

faqs.q: What is the difference between AI Overviews and featured snippets?
faqs.a: A featured snippet quotes one passage from one page. An AI Overview writes a new summary from several sources, often found through related searches, and links to multiple pages.

faqs.q: Can a page appear in both a featured snippet and an AI Overview?
faqs.a: Yes. Both reward direct answers, clear headings and structured content, and both require the page to be indexed and eligible for a snippet.

faqs.q: Do snippet controls affect AI Overviews?
faqs.a: Yes. nosnippet, max-snippet and data-nosnippet limit how your content can be shown in AI features as well as in snippets.

faqs.q: Are AI Overview clicks shown separately in Search Console?
faqs.a: No. Google includes clicks and impressions from AI features in the standard web search totals.
Featured snippets still appear for many queries. AI Overviews appear more often for complex questions, so it pays to optimize for both.
Pages that answer the main question directly, cover the follow-up questions with their own headings, include specific, sourced facts and show clear expertise.
